intro.line: Lorwyn and Shadowmoor have blurred into one eclipsed plane, and a first-year student is lost on it with a campus map.
Past the eclipse lies a university, and past the university a mind that wants to end all suffering by ending the Multiverse as it is.
Recorded: the Echoverse is the newest road. It is still being written.

finale.line: Tam reaches for something older than the multiverses and asks it to undo what was done.
What are the odds? And what would you like them to be?
Emrakul, the Exigent Doom answers, and the two multiverses come apart as quietly as they joined.

villainFinale.line: In this version the Theorist finishes his proof. Every part of him that objected is gone, and the Multiverse is one revision.
The Multiverse is a work in progress. There will need to be revisions.
He thinks he is saving everyone.

battles.title: The Eclipse
battles.blurb: Lorwyn and Shadowmoor blur together, and the sun people have opinions about it.

cards.name: Eirdu, Carrier of Dawn // Isilu, Carrier of Twilight

scene.line: Adherents of the sun implore others to bask in Eirdu's light and expel darkness from the plane.
Blight: put -1/-1 counters on your own creature as a cost. Small creatures are cheap to pay with, big ones are not.

villainScene.line: The scratch became a sore, the sore became a wound, the wound became an infection, and the infection became a funeral.
Shadowmoor creeps in at the edges, and keeps creeping.

hero.half: Pay Blight with your smallest creature.

battles.title: Maralen's Court
battles.blurb: The Faerie Queen of the eclipsed plane rules from a hall of every colour.

deck.name: The Wild Kin of the Creakwood
deck.label: tribute

scene.line: Safewrights stationed within the Creakwood do not fear Shadowmoor's encroaching dark. They embrace it.
Vivid: the more colours among your permanents, the bigger the effect. A two-colour board is already better than a one-colour one.

villainScene.line: This is *my* domain, and *I* am its Queen.
Maralen is more forgiving than Oona was, but her rule is no less absolute.

hero.half: Add a second colour to your board to light Vivid.

battles.title: Oko, Lorwyn Liege
battles.blurb: Oko is back, and this time he has two faces and an entire plane to play with.

cards.name: Oko, Lorwyn Liege // Oko, Shadowmoor Scion

card.name: Oko, Lorwyn Liege // Oko, Shadowmoor Scion

scene.line: Elsewhere in Lorwyn, nestled in a faerie ring, the coos of a small giant turned to cries.
Attack Oko himself. A planeswalker dies the same way a player does, from damage.

villainScene.line: Eclipsed realms are the spaces between Lorwyn's stability and Shadowmoor's chaos
Oko turns your best creature into something small, and then smiles.

hero.half: Attack the planeswalker, not just the player.

battles.title: First-Years
battles.blurb: A student, a campus map and a quiz she is already late for.

scene.line: I don't think we're going to make it back in time for Introduction to Prophecy.
Prepared: a prepared creature lets you cast a copy of its spell once. Hold the creature, keep the spell.

villainScene.line: Strixhaven students have a sense of humor. The spirits of the Blood Age do not.
The rival students are loud, quick and not entirely in control.

hero.half: Cast the copy of the spell on a prepared creature.

battles.title: Strixhaven
battles.blurb: The archaics remember all of history, and some of them are very upset about it.

scene.line: Life is vivid; the pigments I use should be too.
Repartee: when you cast an instant or sorcery that targets a creature, the creature gets a bonus. Aim spells at your own team.

villainScene.line: As the giant shadow loomed, the Forum of Amity fell silent for the first time in its history.
The archaics experience all of Arcavios history, and they are not forgiving.

hero.half: Target your creatures with spells to light Repartee.

battles.title: Witherbloom
battles.blurb: The college of life and death: a swamp, a garden and a very good reputation.

scene.line: If you take the time to listen, the archaics will tell you that this world has been torn asunder and remade many times before.
Witherbloom has deathtouch and flying. Race it, or remove the big one before it connects.

villainScene.line: In most colleges, Erren's poisonous skin would have made them a pariah. In Witherbloom, they were one of the most popular students on campus.
Witherbloom balances the books: what lives pays for what dies.

hero.half: Kill deathtouch creatures before blocking with big ones.

battles.title: The Theorist's Proof
battles.blurb: Jace's lieutenant is checking your work and finding it wanting.

scene.line: If we're going to fix things, we should start here. Why does no one question the Theorist?
Empower puts loyalty counters on a Jace token. The Theorist's deck builds one fast, so be ready to attack it.

villainScene.line: There is no curve. Either you succeeded, or you did not. Either way, this will be informative.
Uldaros Theorix copies what he likes from the graveyard and discards the rest.

hero.half: Attack the Jace token before it grows.

battles.title: The Theorist
battles.blurb: Every part of Jace that objected has been cut away. What is left wants a better Multiverse.

scene.line: Too many lives have been cut short, too many of their futures untold. I can rewrite them. I can give them a voice.
The Theorist draws extra cards and builds Illusions every turn. Do not let him durdle.

villainScene.line: I only wish you could see the necessity of this. Your counterparts all have.
The Multiverse is a work in progress. There will need to be revisions.

hero.half: Pressure the Theorist before his tokens swarm.

battles.title: The Exigent Doom
battles.blurb: Tam calls on something far older than a Theorist, and it answers.

archive.what: A green deck of the set's big creatures, with Emrakul, the Exigent Doom as its top end.
archive.why: It stands for what Tam calls on after the Theorist, and is not a list anyone won with.
archive.beat: Chump the big creatures, keep your life high and win before Emrakul arrives.
archive.after: Nothing; this is the optional superboss at the end of the story.

deck.name: Emrakul and the Echoes
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from cards in this act's sets only. No tournament list is copied.

scene.line: What are the odds? And what would you like them to be?
Race it. Emrakul needs ten mana, and every turn she is late is a turn you are ahead.

villainScene.line: Emrakul does not speak. The Multiverse does it for her.

after.line: Recorded: the two multiverses come apart and Tam finds her way back to class, late as ever.

hero.half: Win before Emrakul reaches ten mana.
